thread:
Maria S.: After upgrading to poetry 1.5 our app started failing imports for the SDK grpc module. Worked before the upgrade.
Redwood Support: Sorry about that — can you paste the exact import error and your install output (poetry/pip)? Also which Python/OS and poetry version?
Maria S.: macOS 13.6, Python 3.11.6, poetry 1.5.1. Repro:
```
poetry new test-repro
cd test-repro
poetry add 'redwood-inference[grpc]'
poetry run python -c "import redwood; import redwood.grpc"
```
Traceback:
```
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'redwood.grpc'
```
I inspected site-packages and found a top-level folder named `redwood_inference` and `redwood_inference-0.9.2.dist-info` — but no `redwood` package.
Lucas (eng): Can you run and paste:
```
ls -la "$(poetry env info -p)/lib/python3.11/site-packages" | sed -n '1,200p'
poetry show --no-dev
```
Maria S.: Pasted full listing to gist: https://gist.github.com/private/ef12gh34 — the wheel we pulled installs `redwood_inference/` not `redwood/`. Historically we had a compatibility shim `redwood/__init__.py` that forwarded to `redwood_inference` but it's missing in this build.
Redwood Support: That matches what we're seeing. Our latest platform-tagged wheel build appears to have dropped the compat shim (the maintainer script in the wheel layout changed). Poetry happily installed the published wheel so your imports break.
Maria S.: We pin `redwood-inference>=0.9.0,<0.10.0` in prod, expecting stable import surface. Any short term advice? CI is failing.
Lucas (eng): Short-term workarounds:
1) Install from sdist (no wheel):
```
pip install --no-binary :all: 'redwood-inference==0.9.2'
```
In a poetry flow you can `poetry run pip install --no-binary :all: redwood-inference==0.9.2` or add the sdist URL as a source. The sdist contains the legacy `redwood/` layout.
2) Pin to the last known-good wheel (if available), e.g. `redwood-inference==0.9.1`.
3) Temporary local shim in your repo (quick but not ideal): create `redwood/__init__.py` that does `from redwood_inference import *` — will restore imports until we publish a fixed wheel.
Maria S.: Doing `--no-binary` fixed the import locally. Thanks. For CI we'd prefer not to modify code.
Redwood Support: We're opening an internal release ticket now. Looks like one of our packager jobs produced a platform-tagged wheel and the compatibility package wasn't included. We'll publish a corrected wheel (or a patch release 0.9.3 with metadata fixed). ETA ~24h, we've escalated.
Maria S.: Appreciate it. Our environments: macOS 13.6 and ubuntu 22.04 in CI, Python 3.11.6, poetry 1.5.1, pip 23.3.1. We also use grpc extras which may pull in platform binaries.
Lucas (eng): FYI: extras like [grpc] sometimes cause the packager to build manylinux wheels with platform tags for the binary deps; those builds sometimes change wheel metadata/layout. If you need grpc, `pip install 'redwood-inference[grpc]==0.9.2' --no-binary :all:` will pull everything from sdist and avoid the problematic wheel.
Redwood Support: We've attached your CI logs and the gist to the ticket and will DM when the fixed wheel is published. :thumbsup:
